Theo: Found an odd parity/dx issue: Kotlin sampleapp's auth flow leaks connections on Android 13+ when cancelling requests during retry.
Rhea: Leak how? stack or quick repro?
Theo: Repro: start a request that triggers a 401, Authenticator kicks off a refresh via a suspend helper, then the UI cancels the call (user navigates away). The underlying Call isn't always cleaned up and connections pile up in the pool.
Omar: Interesting - do you use Call.cancel() or rely on Retrofit cancellation via coroutine Job?
Theo: We use Retrofit suspend adapters so cancellation comes from coroutine cancellation. The token refresh uses a CompletableDeferred single-flight which may hold a reference to the Call if it wasn't detached properly.
Rhea: Might be an ordering issue: OkHttp expects application code to call call.cancel() when coroutine is cancelled. If Authenticator/interceptor holds a strong reference to Call or Response body, cancellation can be delayed.
Theo: Minimal snippet: interceptor runs runBlocking { singleFlightRefresh.await() } to get token, then proceeds. If the coroutine scope is cancelled mid-refresh, our helper doesn't propagate cancel to the ongoing Call used for refresh.
Omar: Fix: ensure the single-flight refresh uses coroutineScope { val job = launch(Dispatchers.IO) { /* perform network */ } coroutineContext.job.invokeOnCompletion { if (it is CancellationException) refreshCall?.cancel() } } and ensure Response.body().close() in finally.
DocsBot: Suggestion: add a "Cancellation & cleanup" note in Kotlin SDK docs and update sampleapp single-flight helper to attach cancel propagation to underlying OkHttp call.
Rhea: Also add a small test in sampleapp that cancels a coroutine during auth refresh and asserts connection pool size doesn't grow.
Theo: I'll open PR with change + unit reproducer. PR #1310 attached.
Omar: Good call. Also add a short note about parity: Java sample uses synchronous refresh so it didn't hit this cancellation path; mention that in docs so engineers know why behavior differs.
DocsBot: Drafted docs blurb: "When bridging suspend refresh into network hooks, propagate cancellation to the underlying OkHttp Call and always close response bodies to avoid connection leaks."
Theo: Thanks, will link logs + small repro in PR. :thumbsup:
